reviews.text: Bueno… este pana y yo vamos a tener problemas. El personaje de Adam Sandler no lo descifro, no sé si es autista, psicopata, no entiendo qué coño es pero no le veo el sentido. Nada de la movie tiene sentido que suceda, no tiene un porqué. El harmonio es cualquiera, los 2 cameos que tiene Phillip Seymour Hoffman son igual de innecesarios y ridículos como su aparición en esta movie. Los flashazos azules pensé que tendrían algún motivo o significado y al parecer es para que se viera “aesthetic” Y no quiero hablar del soundtrack. El peor soundtrack que recuerdo haber escuchado en una película. Inconexo, totalmente contrario pero no logra nada, solo te saca de onda y me deja muy mal sabor de boca. Y bueno la canción del “in it’s me”, prefiero que me rasguen las bolas con un rastrillo a volverla a oír. Nada memorable, nada interesante. Bullshit Este pana está overrated

I would only give ‘Punch Drunk Love’ a 2.5 star rating, because while the film is able to accurately represent a character struggling with social anxiety and repressed rage, the plot is thin and disjointed, making for a confusing and unpleasant watching experience. Certain plot points, such as the pudding scheme and the extortionist brothers' fates fail to resolve, and feel more random than they were likely intended to. It almost feels as though the movie was cut short before it could tie together the story. I personally struggled to maintain focus and understanding as I watched the film. For this reason, I would give the film the relatively low rating of 2.5 stars

I turned this film on to fill up time whilst pining for my boyfriend, he recommended it to me this afternoon on his work break and I'm sorry Fin but this film was a slog. I tried, really did, in theory it should be a perfect film for me; autistic 'literally me' character finds his true love (literally me) with a kooky side plot, good visuals, a great score and Philip Seymour Hoffman. Unfortunately it failed to grip me immediately and then proceeded to continue to struggle and try to grasp onto my brain like a toddler holding a wet fish. It was overly complex with absolutely nothing deep which led to a raging headache an hour in. I paused 30 minutes in to brush my teeth, brushing my teeth was preferable and more important to me than this film!! I really want to like it because the acting is great, the visuals are beautiful, the score is brilliant. I specifically enjoyed a few shots, the first appearance of the blonde guys stepping out of a car, the phone booth lighting up when Barry connects with Lena, the first kiss scene and the second when they meet at the hotel. This film does have merits and yet I had no connection to it, its just left me frustrated because I want to connect with Barry but I couldn't. Maybe it was his violent outbursts to his annoying but ultimately harmless sisters, maybe it's just Adam Sandler (it's not because he's great here and I loved Uncut Gems), maybe it's that his romance is unearned, I'm not sure. Maybe it's a movie for boy autists and I'm too Frances Ha coded fuck knows!! Unlike When Harry Met Sally or Submarine or a litany of other life affirming, love affirming films I've watched that make me cry over my beautiful boyfriend and up the ante on the yearning, this film just left me blank. It all felt so unearned and unbaked and usually I can accept that but it also touts itself as grandiose beyond its means. Maybe I believed the hype too much, maybe I'm not a PTA fan, maybe I'm a faux cinephile, maybe it's just not that great. Watchlist

its da besties bday, so we watch some of da besties fave movies. duh doy. i don't quite think i FULLY understood this movie, but i think that's okay? i just don’t think it was made for ME. i certainly resinated with the whole "i don't like myself sometimes [...] i don't know if there is anything wrong because i don’t know how other people are", but other than that, i felt a little lost on connecting with barry as a character. i will say, i had a knot of anxiety forming in my chest for the entire duration of this movie, and i certainly preferred that over my sense of confusion. i felt as though i was waiting for the final straw to break the camel's (barry’s) back for the better half of the film. the shots that lingered a little too long certainly added to the suspense, but i think it was mostly thanks to the score and soundtrack. it made the entire watching experience so.. uncomfortable? i guess? i mean, using shelley duvall's “he needs me" all the while barry is spiralling and making terrible, manic decisions? absolutely sickening and somehow very excellent. i can understand why people really enjoy this film, but i think it just went right over my stupid little head.

I'm one of those enormous Adam Sandler fans even though most of his roles are just him being himself. But this movie scratched a different itch. Sandler's performance in films like this are always surprising but in the most pleasant way. It's very clear how you feel about Barry from beginning to end - intrigued by the guy, worried for the guy, rooting for the guy. He goes through a tangible personal growth that I think we can all relate to. We all have our own version of his seven sisters that just shape our ugly gremlin we try to hide every day. Finding the thing that pushes it all aside and highlights our greatest qualities is always worth all of the pudding we can afford.

Kişisel olarak Barry ile fazlasıyla empati kurabiliyorum ve bu durum beni oldukça rahatsız ediyor; belki de filmin asıl istediği tam olarak budur. Ailesinin, Barry'nin üzerindeki etkisini hiç fark etmeden onunla sürekli uğraşması, aslında yaşadığı öfke patlamalarını yeterince açıklıyor fakat kimse bunu kabul etmek istemiyor. Barry yapayalnız ve bu yalnızlığı gidermeye çalışıyor; ancak doğru yolları seçemiyor çünkü kendisi de içinde ne taşıdığını tam olarak bilmiyor. Burada kastettiğim ona hak vermek değil, sadece onu anlayabilmek. Yine de kendisini seven, ondan hoşlanan ve ona gerçekten değer veren birini bulduğunda işler toparlanmaya başlıyor; en azından öfkesini doğru yönlendirebiliyor. Film boyunca Barry ne zaman rahatsız hissetse ortam sesleri ve müzikler boğucu bir hâl alıyor, her şey sarpa sarıyor. Biraz olsun rahatladığında ise etraf duruluyor, müzikler sakinleşiyor ve her şey yoluna giriyor. Bu adam yıllarca her şeyi içine atmış, duygularını asla ifade edememiş; şimdi ise eline geçen bu fırsatı nasıl değerlendireceğini bile kestiremiyor. İzlerken fazlasıyla bunaldım ve öfkelendim; zaten filmi bu denli beğenmemin asıl nedeni de tam olarak bu.

Bana yer yer Oslo, August 31st 'ü de anımsattı, hani yer yer onun romantizm versiyonu gibiydi. Fakat ne senaryoyu onun kadar doldurabilmişler, ne de diyalogları. Doğru dönemde izlenince bence insanı olabildiğince etkileyecek bir film. Konusu çok etkili olsa da bence onu aktarmakta yeterince başarılı değil. Adam Sandler wears soothes? Yes, and he plays in a PTA movie. It’s a strong reflection on anxiety and the constant pressure to be accepted by others. PTA made a brilliant and unorthodox choice casting Sandler in this role. In my opinion, it’s his best performance and the one that represents him most truthfully. He’s known as a comedy actor and something of a clown, but he also has a real soul and genuine emotion. Those emotions come through powerfully in the scenes where color floods the screen. He cannot express his emotions and keeps everything inside, so he destroys things because he cannot control himself. That said, the story isn’t really my type. It’s a bit too dreamy, and the sudden shift from his lack of confidence to having the guts to confront the people who hurt him felt exaggerated. And somehow he knows how to fight four blond guys? I’m still not sure what that was all about. Even though there were some aspects I found incoherent, I have to give real appreciation to the cinematography, it’s still flashing in my head. The long tracking shots that move around the character, and the moments where Sandler awkwardly walks toward Lena Leonard (Emily Watson), are simply stunning. The compositions are striking.
